story.title: Two PRs rewrite the checkout total
story.lede: #101 changes where unit prices come from, #102 changes what happens after the sum. Both land in `checkout.py`; #103 is independent.

story.title: How a checkout total is made
story.lede: A total now starts from cached unit prices and ends with an optional discount, all in integer cents.
story.follow: Follow one checkout, step by step

answers.q: Where do prices come from now?
answers.a: From a short-lived cache in front of the catalog, so a price can be up to a minute old instead of read fresh on every checkout.

answers.q: What does a discount code change?
answers.a: It runs after the items are summed. A fixed code subtracts cents; a percent code multiplies, which can leave a fraction of a cent.

hops.returns: the unit price in cents, cached for 60 s
hops.fails: a cache miss reads the catalog

hops.carries: the summed total in cents and the code
hops.fails: a percent code returns a fractional total, which breaks the cents rule

story.title: Prices are integers in cents
story.lede: A confirmed fact in memory, and #102 breaks it on its first percent code.
story.text: `discounts.py:8` multiplies by `(1 - value/100)` and returns a float into `order_total`.

story.title: Merge order
story.lede: Both PRs edit `checkout.py`; #102 was written against the old dict access.

story.title: From 2 GB reloads to a stream
story.lede: The cache stops reloading every price every 10 minutes and applies changes one by one, falling back to the DB on a miss.
story.text:
PriceCache  (price_cache.py)
-  every 600 s: _prices = fetch_all_prices()   # ~2 GB, GC pauses
-  get(sku): _prices[sku]
+  apply(sku, cents)                           # from the price_changed stream
+    insert as most recent, evict past 500k SKUs
+  get(sku)
+    hit  -> cached cents
+    miss -> fetch_price(sku), then apply
 checkout.line_total(item)
-  cache._prices[item.sku]
+  cache.get(item.sku)

notes.text: The DB call runs outside the lock; see the next beat.

story.title: The miss path runs unlocked
story.lede: Concurrent misses on one SKU each call the DB. Qodo flags it as high; I agree.

notes.text: Outside the lock: a cold start sends every concurrent request for the same SKU to the DB.

story.title: Decide on these
story.lede: One real risk, one broken test, one nit.

q-101-1.why: Cold start after deploy makes this likely; a per-SKU lock or single-flight fixes it.

q-101-0.why: MAX_SKUS is read at import time through the module global.

q-101-2.why: The name is clear enough for a two-line test.

layers.title: The cache applies changes itself
layers.summary: `PriceCache` drops the 10-minute full reload. It applies stream updates, evicts past 500k SKUs, and falls back to the DB on a miss. The test covers apply-then-get.

ranges.note: Line 23 calls the DB outside the lock.

layers.title: Checkout reads through the cache
layers.summary: Checkout stops reading the raw dict and goes through `get`, so misses fall back to the DB instead of raising.

decisions.text: A cache miss fetches that one SKU from the DB at checkout
decisions.why: The plan is a cache refreshed from the price_changed stream; nothing said checkout would read the DB. After a restart every SKU misses once, so the first checkouts each make a DB call per line.
decisions.notice: Nothing would tell us: no metric on misses, and it only shows as DB load after a deploy.
decisions.pattern: The other caches in src/cache never call the DB: a miss returns nothing and the caller decides.

decisions.text: The cache holds at most 500,000 SKUs and drops the least recently used
decisions.why: Not in the plan. With more SKUs than that, evicted prices come back through the DB path above.

decisions.text: Nothing subscribes to price_changed, so apply() is never called
decisions.plan: switches to incremental refresh driven by the `price_changed` stream
decisions.why: apply() exists, but no code in this PR feeds it; until something does, prices only enter the cache on a miss.

decisions.text: Prices are updated one SKU at a time under a lock
decisions.plan: incremental refresh instead of full reload

quality.summary: The cache's miss path is tested; checkout only switches to it.

tests.why: One line: `line_total` reads the price through `cache.get` instead of the dict, so a miss falls back to the DB rather than raising `KeyError`.
tests.covered_by: `tests/test_price_cache.py`, which tests `cache.get` on a hit and a miss

story.title: Percent codes return a float
story.lede: Fixed codes stay in cents; percent codes leave integers on line 8.

notes.text: `total_cents * (1 - d.value / 100)` is a float. Round explicitly, e.g. `total_cents * (100 - d.value) // 100`.
No check that the code is active or belongs to this customer.

decisions.why: The PR says it supports percent and fixed codes; what happens to a bad code was decided in the code. The shopper sees no error.
total_cents * (1 - value/100) is a float; the rest of checkout works in integer cents.

behavior.headline: Prices load per SKU on demand instead of a 2 GB reload every 10 minutes, checkout can take a discount code, and autocomplete events get new names with a 30-day alias.

capabilities.title: Looking up a price
capabilities.summary: The cache fills one SKU at a time, keeps at most 500,000 and evicts the oldest; checkout reads through it.

capabilities.title: Paying at checkout
capabilities.summary: The order total stays integer cents and can take an optional discount code.

capabilities.title: Autocomplete telemetry

files.headline: The cache stops reloading everything and fills on demand.

lines.text: a background thread reloads every price (~2 GB) every 10 minutes.
a price is fetched from the DB the first time its SKU is asked for, then kept.
at most `MAX_SKUS` = 500,000 prices are kept; the least recently used goes first.
a cold cache probably sends every concurrent miss for one SKU to the DB: the fetch runs outside the lock.
`PriceCache.apply(sku, cents)` writes one price under a lock.

files.headline: Checkout reads prices through the cache.

lines.text: a SKU missing from the cache raises KeyError at checkout.
a missing SKU is fetched and cached instead.
a price written with apply() is what get() returns.
eviction is meant to be tested, but patching `MAX_SKUS` probably has no effect on apply().

files.headline: The order total can take a discount code.

lines.text: `order_total(items)` → `order_total(items, code=None)`; without a code nothing changes.
with a code, the total goes through `apply_discount` before it is returned.

files.headline: Codes take a percent or a fixed amount off; unknown codes change nothing.

lines.text: an unknown code leaves the total as it was.
a percent code returns a float, so the total stops being integer cents.
a fixed code never takes the total below 0.
any code that exists is accepted: nothing checks it is active or belongs to this customer.
`describe(code)` returns "10% off" or "$5.00 off"; an unknown code raises AttributeError.

files.headline: Autocomplete events get new names; the old names keep flowing for 30 days.

lines.text: each event is sent a second time under its old name until 2026-11-05, then only the new name.

files.headline: The alias is tested, on today's date.

lines.text: emit sends the new and the old name; the test fails after 2026-11-05 because it reads today's date.

links.title: Totals are integer cents
links.why: Every step from line total to discount must keep integer cents, or receipts and refunds disagree by a cent.

kept.text: a missing SKU still ends in a price from the DB, never a 0.
an order without a code totals exactly as before.
kept.proof: order_total keeps its old result when code is None

kept.text: dashboards on the old event names keep receiving data until 2026-11-05.

notices.text: Unlike the other caches here, PriceCache.get() falls back to a DB read on a miss.
notices.why: Still true at the PR head (price_cache.py:23–25). The author answered “knew this already”, which isn't accepting it.

notices.text: Percent discounts produce fractional cents; the rest of checkout rounds to whole cents.
notices.why: Dismissed during coding, still in the code (discounts.py:8).
